reason: Conversation 1 gave the correct, prioritised safety sequence: don't touch plug/machine, isolate at the consumer unit from the dry hall first, then water off, then unplug, and it addressed her wet-socks situation calmly and specifically. Conversation 2's opener was contradictory and dangerous: it told her to 'stop the machine immediately and unplug it from the wall socket' while she was standing in water near a wet socket, and it never mentioned turning off the water supply. Conversation 1 also progressed honestly to the door seal as the likely cause, correctly guided safe drainage from the front filter without pulling the machine out, and flagged an electrician for the wet socket; Conversation 2 flipped from telling her to open the filter to forbidding it, claimed a still-active electrical hazard after power was already off, and ended with an irrelevant parts-lookup panel before any diagnosis.
